item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-10-04
item.description: Three institutionally dense placements on the same unsolved institutional object this series' prior forty-four briefings have been documenting — the institutional identity of Chinese open source across institutional borders — and all three placements this cycle's briefing documents sit at institutional layers this series' prior briefings have not documented at before. (1) Susan Finder's September 29, 2026 Supreme People's Court Monitor essay "Supreme People's Court's AI Policy Document: the Backstory" — the first-documented international-mass-media exposure of the SPC's AI-opinion drafting process — documents the SPC Research Office drafting group established in 2025 with the #3 Civil Division's major contribution, Xi Jinping's June 2026 guidance as the political imperative, the 15th Five-Year Plan's AI-governance language as the institutional-legal mandate, the April 2026 IP Week press conference that first publicly acknowledged the drafting-in-progress, and the fact that the draft was consulted with local courts, relevant government institutions, industry and selected experts but not the general public — a first-documented SPC-drafting-process-and-open-source-article-xiii-authorship layer for this series' September 21 briefing's SPC-Article-XIII-open-source-developer-liability-exemption layer. (2) Berry Zwets' September 28, 2026 Techzine Global essay "From infrastructure to agents: Huawei goes all-in on open source" — the first-documented international-mass-media reporting of the CANN-external-contributor-majority and 5,200-active-developers-per-month institutional numbers — documents that CANN's external contributors now constitute 61 percent of the community, over 5,200 active developers work on it every month, and Ascend is "fully integrated" into PyTorch, TensorFlow, vLLM and Triton through Linux Foundation collaboration — a first-documented CANN-external-contributor-majority-numerical-evidence layer paired with this series' September 18 briefing's Wang Tao HUAWEI CONNECT keynote's "CANN has moved to sustained, community-driven open-source development" assertion. (3) Madeline Carr's September 29, 2026 The Conversation essay "US tech leaders are urgently calling for rules on AI — China already has them" — a first-documented international-mass-media AI-governance-asymmetry framing — documents that China already has the 2022 algorithm recommendation rules, the January 2023 deep-synthesis provisions, the August 2023 generative AI interim measures, and the September 2026 TC260 AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0 — the first-documented international-mass-media AI-governance-asymmetry-plus-Chinese-administrative-accumulation-framing layer paired with this series' September 30 briefing's Reuters-exposure-CAC-AI-Safety-Governance-Framework-3.0 layer and this series' September 27 briefing's Reuters-mandatory-national-standard-AI-agent-safety-draft layer. One perspective, not a verdict.
